NovaBio Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Thompson, Head of Commercial.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaBio Therapeutics.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBio Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust momentum from our new product launches and expanding portfolio in oncology and rare diseases, which fueled 28% year-over-year revenue growth. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

I'm particularly pleased to update you on our new product launches, which have been the cornerstone of this quarter's success and are positioning us for ongoing market share gains against major competitors such as Merck's Keytruda and Bristol Myers Squibb's Opdivo. Let me highlight NovaCetux, our PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody approved for frontline non-small cell lung cancer, or NSCLC, and BioVira, our AAV-based gene therapy for hemophilia A.

NovaCetux gained FDA approval in late Q2 following the pivotal Phase III NOVALUNG-301 trial, which showed a statistically significant 42% improvement in progression-free survival—a median PFS of 14.2 months compared to 9.8 months in the Keytruda-pembrolizumab control arm, with a p-value below 0.0001 and an 18% reduction in grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events. Launch uptake has exceeded expectations: in its first full quarter, it posted $178 million in net U.S. sales, beating our $140-160 million guidance. IQVIA NPA data indicates this captures about 12% of the total U.S. NSCLC PD-1 market.

Among new patient starts, or NRx, we've secured 22% share of U.S. frontline PD-(L)1 initiations, gaining 8 points sequentially from Q2 and taking 4 points from Keytruda, whose NRx share fell to 52% from 56%. Total Rx, or TRx, share is at 15%, bolstered by 92% persistence at month 3 versus the category's 85% average. This stems from our account-based strategy, with over 1,200 key opinion leader engagements and access to 85% of NCCN-designated cancer centers. We've achieved a wholesale acquisition cost of $168,000 per patient-year, with average selling prices at 92% of WAC after rebates, aided by formulary positions at CVS Caremark and Express Scripts covering 70% of commercial lives.

While the U.S. drives 95% of sales, EMA approval is on track for Q1 2025 with bridged data from the EU-focused NOVALUNG-302 trial. In China, our Sinopharm collaboration has advanced, with an NMPA filing in November and early access in 15 tier-1 hospitals, forecasting $25 million in APAC royalties by year-end. The global NSCLC PD-1 market topped $28 billion in 2023 per Evaluate Pharma, and our bispecific profile shines in squamous histology with 28% NRx share.

Manufacturing has scaled at our North Carolina site to 50,000 doses monthly, with CHO-K1 optimizations cutting COGS to 22% of sales. A subcutaneous version showed matching pharmacokinetics to intravenous in Phase I data at ESMO recently, with a BLA planned for the second half of 2025 to improve convenience.

BioVira, our one-time treatment for severe hemophilia A launched in U.S. Q1 post-BLA, reached $92 million in sales, up 65% sequentially from 86 to 142 treated patients. Symphony Health data shows 11% share in the U.S. hemophilia A switcher segment, gaining 6 points from Roche's Hemlibra at 72%, thanks to 95% mean six-month ABR reduction in real-world data from expanded access.

Payer support is strong at 88% commercial coverage, including a J-code for reimbursements. In Europe, we've set pricing at €1.8 million, matching BioMarin's Roctavian, with HTA nods in Germany and UK NICE innovative pathways. Takeda partnership rolls out in Japan Q4 2024, eyeing 20% of 1,200 eligible patients.

These efforts align with our precision portfolio, including NovaCetux combos with legacy CDK4/6 NovaKira in HR+/HER2- breast cancer showing 68% ORR early. We forecast NovaCetux peak at $4.2 billion by 2028, BioVira $1.1 billion, supporting 2025 revenue guidance of $1.2-1.4 billion and 25-30% operating margins. Supply challenges raised inventory to 145 days, but dual Indian CDMO sourcing helps. We're watching Opdivo expansions, but head-to-head data protects us in high PD-L1 cases.

Overall, these launches affirm our R&D and execution, prompting an EPS raise to $2.15-2.35.

Now, I will turn the call over to Michael Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex noted, we had a solid quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.52 billion, an increase of 18% on a reported basis and 19% at constant exchange rates compared to $2.13 billion in Q3 2023. This marks our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth, propelled by volume gains, modest pricing, and geographic shifts to higher-margin ex-U.S. regions. Excluding a $150 million PD-1 milestone, core growth was 16% CER. U.S. sales were $1.71 billion, up 17%, with ex-U.S. at $810 million, up 20% CER.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $2.10 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $520 million, or $2.45 per share.

Turning to product revenue by key franchises—oncology, immunology, and rare diseases—worldwide net product sales hit $2.52 billion. Oncology led at $1.28 billion, up 22% CER or 51% of portfolio, driven by OncoZor anti-PD-1 at $1.15 billion, up 24% CER. Volume contributed 19 points with TRx up 21% to 285,000 and NRx up 28% to 95,000, securing 32% U.S. NSCLC share per IQVIA, up from 27%, despite biosimilar competition. Persistence is 78% at 12 months via RWE in combos with NovaLink-301.

U.S. ASP rose 3% to $48,200 per patient-year post-rebates, offset by 340B at 28% volume and GTN at 52%. Ex-U.S., ASP up 7% CER in Japan and Germany. U.S. $820 million up 20%, Europe $250 million up 30% CER on MSI-high expansion, EM $80 million up 35% led by China. Singapore fill-finish supports 120,000 vials monthly.

Immunology at $920 million, up 14% CER, with ImmunoGuard IL-4/13 at $890 million up 15%. Volume drove 12 points: TRx +14% to 420,000, NRx +18% to 112,000 in AD adult/pediatric. U.S. AD share steady at 24% vs. Dupixent biosimilars. Adherence 82% at six months. U.S. ASP +4% to $22,500 amid 48% GTN; ex-U.S. flat CER offset by China NRDL volume.

U.S. $650 million +13%, Europe $190 million +16% CER NICE, Japan/EM $80 million +22%. ImmunoGuard 2.0 bispecific in Phase 3 eyes 2038 exclusivity, 20% volume via SC/IV.

Rare diseases $320 million +28% CER, RareGen SMA Type 1 $310 million +30%. Volume +25 points: 1,420 global starts—U.S. 850 +22%, Europe 420 +35% presymptomatic, Japan 150 +50%. 92% treated within six months post-diagnosis via screening mandates.

U.S. ASP -1% to $2.15 million on 340B/outcomes rebates; ex-U.S. +5% CER. AAV9 scale-up to 5,000 doses/year; Q4 DMD launch eyes $200 million peak by 2027.

Volume grew 17% vs. IQVIA 12%, via 15 label expansions, MyNovaBio app +10% NRx. Pricing +3% CER despite 49% GTN, IRA. Ex-U.S. 32% sales up from 28%.

Priorities: biosimilar defense via ADCs/bispecifics +5% share; AI manufacturing COGS -15% FY25; $500 million BD for three Phase 3 2025 readouts. Q4 revenue $2.6-2.7 billion, FY $10.1-10.3 billion +17-18% CER.

Operating expenses totaled $248 million, up 14% year-over-year or 180 basis points above guidance midpoint, at 82% of revenue? Wait, no—actually about 10% reflecting revenue scale, up from prior due to R&D push. R&D was $182 million, 73% of OpEx, +22% YoY, flat sequentially. Drives: Phase III BNT-347 HER2 bispecific 850+ patients 120 sites; BNT-512 SMA Phase II post-FDA IND.

CMC scale at Lonza for H1 2025 BLAs +$25 million; NVIDIA BioNeMo AI cuts screening 35%, three preclinical INDs. R&D headcount +8% to 420 FTEs, $60 million monthly burn, 28-month runway post-$450 million raise.

65% U.S., 20% Cambridge UK MHRA ILAP, 15% APAC WuXi for BNT-347 China bridges vs. IRA caps.

SG&A $56 million +4% YoY, 23% OpEx down from 27%, sales/marketing $18 million +12% for BNT-289 Fabry ERT at 18% U.S. share vs. Fabrazyme. 10% U.S. field attrition to EU5. G&A $38 million incl. $12 million SBC, SAP upgrade vs. 15% excipient inflation.

Other $10 million Devens fill-finish for ADCs vs. Catalent constraints.

Efficiency: 15-20% 2024 via IQVIA RWE, Medidata virtual trials -40% activation. Path to non-GAAP profit 2026 on BNT-347 $1.2 billion peak.

Q4 OpEx $255-265 million, R&D $190 million; FY $980 million +16%.

On pricing and reimbursement, U.S. 62% revenue saw 2% QoQ net price gain for NovaTrast HER2 ADC despite IRA. NovaKIR kinase negotiation 2026 models 25-40% GTN hit on $18,500 WAC; Flatiron RWE PFS edge aids CMS LCDs.

ASP Q3 -4.2% YoY on 48% 340B +32% PBM rebates NovaTrast; 15% VBA lives rebate 8% vs. 22%. PAPs cover 28,000 patients $180 million bad debt.

Europe 22% revenue: Germany AMNOG PMP 20% rebate cap €12,400 NovaTrast €2.1 billion 2023; France ASMR IV 15% cut offset CDAs 92% net; UK NICE ICER £48,000/QALY ELEVATE 1.7 QALY modeling.

Horizon HTA accelerator -4-6 months IQWiG. Biosimilars hit NovaMab TNF -31% volume ASP -22% $1,200; divested immunology focus oncology.

Ex-U.S./EM 16%: Japan SAKIGAKE ¥1.85 million NovaTrast; China NRDL 72% WAC RMB 850 million 45% YoY Guangdong 88% wins; Brazil CMED R$45,000 CONITEC RWE.

Trends: GLP-1 scrutiny ADC cuts; gene therapy VBAs like Zolgensma installments; biosimilar HTA 25% cap 2027.

PCE AI 10,000 scenarios 4.5% WAC hikes <5.9% SSR; Verana RWE; PhRMA IRA rare carve-outs NovaHIF ODACP.

FY24 U.S. net 78% WAC flat, FY25 3-5% erosion; EU5 85% NovaTrast; ex-U.S. 22% CAGR NRDL. $250 million payer innovation protects $4.5 billion.

Cash, equivalents, investments $2.8 billion end-Q3, +15% QoQ +45% YoY, top-quartile peers. Net cash $1.9 billion post-$900 million debt <4% fixed to 2028, 0.4x net debt/EBITDA.

Assets $6.2 billion +12% YoY SynthoGen $450 million intangibles; working capital $2.1 billion DSO 52 days; inventory 7.2 months 5.1x turns NovaGLP-2 stock; equity $4.5 billion +18% $250 million repurchases BVPS $28.50 +22%.

Ops cash YTD $850 million x2 YoY, Q3 $620 million; adj $730 million FCF $390 million post-$230 million capex. Gross margins 82% NovaGLP-1 65% revenue.

U.S. $550 million +35% NovaGLP-1 formulary; Europe/ex-U.S. $210 million +50% NovaCAR-301 tenders -$30 million FX hedge 70%; APAC $90 million Takeda Keytruda biosimilar.

Investing $520 million: $300 million NC perfusion CAR-T -40% costs; $150 million gene therapy in-license.

Financing -$400 million repurchases/dividends debut signal $4.5-5.0 billion FY guide 25-30% EPS.

Priorities: $200 million NovaAI NVIDIA halving Phase 1; $150 million Singapore biosimilars 15% $100B; 3+ year runway.

For full year, we update guidance to revenue $10.1-10.3 billion, 17-18% CER growth.

R&D expenses hit $452 million Q3, +14% YoY from $397 million, TTM $1.78 billion ~28% revenue peer-aligned Regeneron/Vertex. Seq +8% late-stage enrollment CMC.

Clinical 62% $280 million +18% Phase 2/3; preclinical 25% $113 million; enabling 13%. 35% CRO IQVIA/PPD, 4.2-year runway post-$1.2 billion notes.

Oncology 42% $190 million +20%: BNT-301 PD-1/VEGF Phase 3 NSCLC 1,200 patients 150 sites 68% ORR PD-L1 $4 billion peak; ADC BNT-215 HER2 Phase 2 $45 million.

Immunology 28% $126 million +12%: BNT-142 subQ IL-23 psoriasis/Crohn's 75% Phase 3 ENLIGHTEN-2 Q4 data cleaner Tremfya. Rare 15% $68 million AAV9 Pompe/Fabry BNT-078 IND.

CNS/cardiometabolic 15%: BNT-095 ASO ALS Wave GalNAc $35 million NPV $2.8 billion.

Digital $52 million Recursion BioHive-2 -40% hit-lead 1.2 million compounds 5 Phase 1. CGT 30% pipeline in vivo CAR-T 85% regression; mRNA 8% LNP oncology.

55% U.S. Cambridge MA; 25% Europe Munich EMA adaptive; 20% APAC WuXi NSCLC 30% enrollment -25% timelines hedge IRA 45% ex-U.S. peak.

Prioritize >$1 billion peak >35% PoS: terminated two IO save $40 million; $300 million Gilead bispecifics.

FY24 R&D $1.85-1.95 billion +10-12%, Q3 milestone-heavy; $150 million capex vectors.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Michael. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. In oncology, BNT-301 NSCLC Phase 3 is advancing rapidly with strong enrollment, building on Phase 2 ORR data. BNT-347 HER2 breast cancer Phase 3 has exceeded 850 patients, on track for H1 2025 BLA. Rare disease efforts include BNT-512 SMA Phase II initiation and BNT-078 Fabry/Pompe IND clearance. Immunology's BNT-142 Phase 3 is 75% enrolled for Q4 topline. We expect multiple milestones in Q4, including NOVALUNG-302 EU data and ImmunoGuard 2.0 interim safety.

Next, Dr. Raj Patel will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Elena. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Preclinical advancements include AI-optimized screening yielding three IND candidates via NVIDIA BioNeMo, cutting cycles 35%. Our AAV9 platform scales for gene therapies, with 40% yield boosts. In vivo CAR-T for solid tumors shows 85% regression in models, and ADC portfolio like BNT-215 leverages proprietary linkers. mRNA LNP vaccines and ASO for ALS with Wave tech are progressing. We're prioritizing multi-omics for novel targets in CNS and cardiometabolic, with five Phase 1-ready assets.

Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Thompson, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Lisa Thompson, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Raj. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with strong uptake in NovaCetux at 22% NRx share and BioVira 65% sequential growth to 11% switcher market. OncoZor NSCLC prescriptions surged 28% NRx, ImmunoGuard AD stabilized share with digital tools boosting adherence. RareGen SMA hit record patient starts via newborn screening. Marketing campaigns, including KOL networks and MyNovaBio app, drove 10% NRx lift, with EU5 expansions and China tenders accelerating ex-U.S. We are seeing robust demand in high-margin segments, optimizing field force for launches.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Lisa. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On NovaCetux, can you elaborate on the sustainability of the 22% NRx share given Keytruda's dominance, and any early combo data with NovaKira?

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thanks, John. The 22% NRx is driven by superior PFS and safety from NOVALUNG-301, plus 85% NCCN access and 92% persistence. We're gaining in squamous NSCLC at 28%. Early HR+/HER2- breast combos with NovaKira show 68% ORR, with Phase II advancing.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen, JPMorgan:
Great, thanks. Michael, on the pricing side, how are you modeling IRA impact on NovaKIR, and VBA performance?

Michael Chen, CFO:
Emily, we've modeled 25-40% GTN for 2026 negotiation on $18,500 WAC, mitigated by Flatiron RWE PFS data. VBAs for NovaTrast rebated only 8% vs. 22% modeled, covering 15% lives tied to OS.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee, Morgan Stanley:
Thanks. Elena, updates on BNT-301 Phase 3 timeline and enrollment?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:
David, BNT-301 frontline NSCLC Phase 3 has enrolled 1,200 across 150 sites, on track post-Phase 2 68% ORR in PD-L1 high. Topline H2 2026, BLA 2027 targeting $4 billion peak.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim, Bank of America:
Thanks. Lisa, commercial thoughts on RareGen DMD Q4 launch ramp?

Lisa Thompson, Head of Commercial:
Rachel, DMD leverages SMA success with newborn mandates, AAV9 scale to 5,000 doses, payer J-codes. Targeting $200 million peak 2027 via EU HTA and Japan PMDA.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Oncology $1.28B (+22% CER): OncoZor $1.15B (+24%), volume +19 pts (TRx +21%, NRx +28%), US ASP +3% to $48.2k, ex-US +7%. Immunology $920M (+14%): ImmunoGuard $890M (+15%), volume +12 pts (TRx +14%, NRx +18%), US ASP +4% to $22.5k, ex-US flat. Rare diseases $320M (+28%): RareGen $310M (+30%), volume +25 pts, US ASP -1% to $2.15M, ex-US +5%. Overall volume +17%, pricing +3% CER.

Europe: Germany AMNOG 20% rebate cap, France ASMR IV 15% cut, UK NICE £48k/QALY. Ex-US: Japan SAKIGAKE, China NRDL 72% WAC, Brazil CMED. Assets $6.2B (+12% YoY), equity $4.5B (+18%), DSO 52 days, inventory 7.2 months. Ops cash Q3 $620M/YTD $850M (+2x YoY), adj FCF $390M (capex $230M), gross margins 82%. $250M repurchases.

Priorities: AI/NVIDIA (35% screening cut), CMC scale/Lonza, in vivo CAR-T, ADC/bispecifics, terminations saved $40M; 28-month runway.
